claims.text: The as-deposited material is an FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayer with nanoscale layers.
The initial multilayer exhibits compositional complexity and severe lattice distortion.
The initial multilayer has a modest degree of short-range order.
Controlled annealing can enhance short-range order specifically at the FCC/BCC interfaces.
The annealing treatment can enhance interfacial short-range order without altering the nanoscale multilayer architecture.
Enhanced interfacial short-range order is the predominant governor of progressive plastic deformation under sustained load.
Greater interfacial short-range order increases the effectiveness of dislocation pinning.
Dislocation pinning under sustained load causes dislocations to accumulate at the interfaces.
Interfacial dislocation pile-ups create localized stress concentrations.
The localized stress concentrations caused by dislocation pile-ups promote creep-driven plastic deformation.
At otherwise identical creep-activating loading conditions, annealed multilayers will show more interfacial dislocation accumulation than as-deposited controls.
At otherwise identical creep-activating loading conditions, annealed multilayers will have a higher progressive creep deformation rate than as-deposited controls.
The predicted increase in creep rate is caused by enhanced dislocation trapping at the more ordered interfaces.
The proposed mechanism applies when loading is sustained at a constant creep-activating temperature and the nanoscale multilayer structure remains intact.
